things.label: Shutter
lines: The shutter is down. Rust has locked the bottom slats to the sill.

things.label: Water tank
lines: AGUA, painted by hand. Under it, older letters, painted by a different hand.
The pipe down the leg is sweating. The ground under it is green.

things.label: Goats
lines: Four goats in a pen made of somebody’s fence and somebody else’s gate.

things.label: Platform
lines: A shroud on the boards, sewn shut with white thread.

things.label: Flags
lines: Seven flags on seven poles. The colors have all gone the same gray-pink.

things.label: Well
lines: The bucket comes up wet. Somebody's lucky night.

things.label: Table
lines: A long table outside the chapel. The bench on the near side is worn smooth.

things.label: Cellar door
lines: A steel hatch in the yard behind the school. Under it, steps going down into the dark.

things.label: Big Store
lines: A store the size of a field. The doors are chained, but not the loading dock round the side.

things.label: Warehouse
lines: Tin walls, three stories of nothing. Something big was kept in here once.

things.label: Old bench
lines: A concrete bench by the trail. A heart carved in the seat, the letters worn off.

things.label: Swing
lines: A swing on a frame. The seat is new. The chains are not.

things.label: Chalk drawing
lines: A chalk drawing on the shed wall: a sun, a house, and something with too many legs.

things.label: Machine
lines: A small machine on four wheels, mowing the same square of dead grass it always has.

things.label: Culvert
lines: The drain goes under the road here. The pipe is black all the way in. Something in there drips.

things.label: Concrete pipe
lines: A pipe as tall as a man, where the creek used to go under the road. Something lives in it. The sand at its mouth is swept.

things.label: Barricade
lines: Del Mar runs into the highway’s wall. Somebody stacked barriers across what’s left of it.

things.label: On-ramp
lines: The ramp climbs up onto the Thirty-Five. Up there, the highway goes north out of town.

things.label: Barricade
lines: Barriers across Del Mar and a car on its side. Past it, the road goes east toward the lake.

things.label: Sign
lines: A highway sign, face down in the caliche.
Underneath, where the sun never reached, the letters are still white: NORTH 35. SAN ANTONIO 154.

things.label: Gantry
lines: A steel frame over the ramp. Something on it turns to watch whatever passes. A red light says STOP.

things.label: Overpass
lines: An overpass, half of it down across the southbound lanes, rebar hanging out of the break like roots.
The other half still stands, carrying nothing.

things.label: Door
lines: Shut. Cool air comes from under it.

things.label: Stones
lines: Stones stacked waist high, bleached white. Bones between them, set with care.

things.label: Canopy
lines: A roof on four legs over dead pumps. Open on every side.

things.label: Culvert
lines: The drain goes under the road here. The pipe is black all the way in. Something in there drips.

things.label: Billboard
lines: A billboard on two legs. Paper on paper on paper, all of it peeled. Not one word left.

things.label: Light
lines: Green, then yellow, then red. Then green again.

things.label: Tracks
lines: Little tracks in the dust. Six wheels. They come up out of the drain and go east.

things.label: Stones
lines: Stones stacked waist high, bleached white. Bones between them, set with care.

things.label: Yard
lines: Cars stacked on cars, every door gone, every hood gone. The fences in town came from here.

things.label: Tower
lines: A concrete tower standing out in the white. Halfway up, a dark band all the way round. Above it, the concrete is pale.

things.label: Buoy
lines: A buoy on its side on the dry bed. Every few breaths, its lamp blinks.

things.label: Boat
lines: A boat, sitting level on the crust as if it were floating.

things.label: Ramp
lines: A concrete ramp runs down into the bowl, and keeps going, under the crust.

things.label: Tracks
lines: Two treads, wide as a door, with cross-bars. They cross the whole bowl.

things.label: Dam
lines: A long bank of earth along the west side, a concrete lip along its top. On this side, nothing to hold.
